To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the free-standing liberal-arts college, as a distinct type of higher educational institution, is in a state of transition and that the future is uncertain.

(1) the American liberal arts colleges are in a period of rapid change, (2) the change is being driven by the external environment, (3) the change is occurring in the context of a long-term decline in resources and a concomitant decline in the number of students attending the colleges, (4) colleges have responded to this change by changing their programs, (5) the changes in programs have not been sufficient to stem the decline in resources and enrollments, (6)
the free-standing liberal art college is in a state of crisis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the colleges are changing and how they are responding to change.
the survival of liberal arts colleges.

a number of issues that are central to the survival of the liberal arts colleges: (a) the nature and quality of faculty work and its relation to the quality of the student experience, (b) the quality and nature of the student experience as it affects the quality of the college's product, (c) the quality of the institutional environment and how this environment affects the quality of faculty and student work.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the liberal arts colleges have not been able to adapt to the changing environment.
liberal arts colleges, as a group, have not adapted to the new economic, political, social, and educational environment.
the liberal arts college is not in a position to be able to respond to the challenges of the 1980's.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the liberal arts college is in a precarious situation.
we are witnessing a time of great transition and uncertainty for the liberal arts college, but that the colleges themselves are not in imminent danger of extinction.
, while we have not yet reached the point of despair, the future is far from assured.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liberal arts college is in a period of rapid and significant change.
we need to understand the liberal arts college in terms of the people who make it up and in terms of the context within which it is situated.
the liberal arts colleges of today face a set of challenges and opportunities that are different from those faced by colleges of yesterday.
